home-dotfiles/RTK.md states as a rule 'always prefix shell commands with rtk' and the binary was absent until today, so every command run before then violated a rule in our own dotfiles
Decide rtk-bash-guard.sh: deploy it, or delete the rule and the guard. A mandatory prefix nobody can enforce is the worst of the three
Add JuliusBrussee/caveman to the RTK prior-art record as the named alternative

epics.title: EPIC: Supply-chain verification so adopting new tools is safe rather than refused
epics.body_intro: Position corrected 2026-07-30. Refusing `curl | sh` is not a policy, it is the absence of one, and it blocks adoption of a field that moves weekly. The operator's framing is right: use the open-source equivalents of JFrog Artifactory and Xray, then adopt safely. RTK was installed correctly the same day (release zip, SHA256 verified against the published checksums file, e9f2e26c...). Oak was refused because its documented install is a pipe to a shell. The difference between those two outcomes should be a process, not a mood.
tasks: tools/supply/verify.py: record provenance (source URL, sha256, size, signature status, scanner verdict, decision, ts) to an append-only state/supply-chain.jsonl, and REFUSE to mark an artifact adopted with no recorded hash. Selftest plus mutation entry per the repo's four-layer convention

Evaluate and pick from the open-source Xray equivalents: Trivy, Grype plus Syft for SBOM, OSV-Scanner, cargo-audit, cargo-deny, cargo-vet, pip-audit, and sigstore cosign with SLSA provenance for signing
ADR stating the rule for a pipe-to-shell install: when it is acceptable, what the substitute is, and what evidence must exist before an artifact counts as adopted
A supply_chain domain in quality-contract.json so an unverified artifact FAILS the gate rather than passing because nobody looked
Backfill what is already installed: rtk.exe (hash on record), the claude-plugins-official marketplace clone, and whatever the WSL2 migration installs
Then reopen Oak against a verified artifact path, because the objection was never the tool and the operator is right that we cannot avoid adopting the new scene

epics.title: EPIC: Point-in-time reconstruction for state that has no history
epics.body_intro: ABSORB-02, deferred on 2026-07-25 as roughly 150 lines to be built 'only when a concrete need appears'. The need appeared three times in one session, which is the argument for building it now rather than the argument for deferring again.
tasks: Driver 1: the review domain's waiver in quality-contract.json changed mid-session from 'until 2026-08-12' to 'until 2026-08-02' with an entirely different stated reason, and nothing on disk can say when it changed or by what

Driver 2: tools/review/panel.py line 11 asserted 'the codex binary is not installed' while codex-cli 0.146.0 was installed and ChatGPT-authenticated, for an unknown length of time, and two subagents read it as fact during one session

Driver 3: a git-repo census reported 1,870 repositories. 1,884 directories were our own leaked test fixtures and the true count is 28, so every conclusion drawn from that walk came from a number our own broken test produced

tools/timetravel/snapshot.py: content-addressed snapshots of the GITIGNORED ledgers with a committed manifest, so a ledger's value at a past moment is recoverable. Do not rebuild what git already gives for tracked files

The original need is still open and belongs to another lane: hiring_engine/ledger.sqlite holds 272 jobs, 4 applications and 21 approvals with zero history. That is a proposal row from here, not this lane's work

epics.title: EPIC: The prose gate measures the ruled form, not the property
epics.body_intro: L-2026-07-31-b. The operator read a 5.4k-word deliverable that had passed tools/slop_lint.py and said it read as machine written, naming dashes. Measured: zero em dashes, zero en dashes, two non-ASCII characters in the file and both were quoted from the artifact under review. So the accusation was falsifiable and false, and the intuition behind it was still pointing at something the gate cannot see: hyphen-compound density 2.8 percent and sentence-length standard deviation 14.8. voice-metrics/SKILL.md:21 already classifies no-em-dashes as RULED, a decision with no corpus behind it. The harness gates the ruled proxy and leaves the measured property ungated, the same shape as L-2026-07-29-g.
tasks: Port a hyphen-density and sentence-length-variance check from ~/.claude/skills/voice-metrics/voice_score.py into tools/slop_lint.py
Fit the thresholds against the operator's own corpus (n=35,472 messages, voice-metrics profiles.json). Do not guess them; a guessed threshold is a second ruled rule wearing a number
Regression tests in both directions: a file that passes today and reads as generated must go red, and the operator's own prose must stay green
Mutation control proving the new check can go red, per the repo's four-layer standard
Warn before it blocks. Collect a week of scores first, then decide the threshold from the distribution rather than from taste
Until this lands, stop citing a clean slop_lint as evidence that prose does not read as generated. It is evidence of one banned list and one dash rule

2026-07-31 measured: tools/slop_lint.py has NO notion of fenced code blocks. Confirmed by reading it, no fence handling and no backtick handling anywhere. It lints mermaid diagrams and code samples as prose, so docs/SYSTEM-MAP.md carries 5 unfixable hits inside its diagram's subgraph labels. Same false-positive class as panel.py (L-2026-07-29-d), in this repo's own prose gate. Regression test must pin a dash inside a fence as CLEAN and the identical dash outside it as a HIT.
2026-07-31 measured: docs/INDEX.md, the docs-control-plane spine, had 43 em-dash hits and was never linted by anything. The prose gate exists and is not bound to the documents.

epics.title: EPIC: A waiver's reason must name the mechanism its falsifier tests
epics.body_intro: L-2026-07-31-a. The review domain carried a waiver through three renewals whose stated reason was that the blocking findings were matches against comments and docstrings. Measured 2026-07-30, that reason was wrong for all five. The waiver shipped its own falsifier, an AST walk of the final file, and it PASSED. It passed for a different reason than the one written beside it, which launders a wrong diagnosis into an audited one. A falsifier that cannot distinguish its stated mechanism from every other reason the same command could pass is not a falsifier.
tasks: DONE 2026-07-31: both underlying defects fixed in tools/review/panel.py; waiver replaced with one that records the old reason as wrong; panel 5 high to 0 high
The review waiver expires 2026-08-02 and committing this branch is what clears it. Decide before then: commit, or renew with a reason that is true
Audit every other waiver in quality-contract.json against the same test: does the reason name a mechanism, and can its falsifier tell that mechanism from the alternatives
Report a waiver past its second renewal as a class rather than as a fresh decision. Three renewals happened here before anyone re-read the reason
Audit the 1,260 lines drop_stale_lines now removes (75,932 to 74,672 reviewed). Each should be a line the tree does not contain at the claimed position; none has been checked individually

epics.title: EPIC: Review work must recompute its own numbers and render what it judges
epics.body_intro: L-2026-07-31-c. An 11k-word review of two external artifacts presented about fifteen measured quantities in the same flat voice as its inferences. An independent recount with no access to the reasoning found four wrong, including a decimal-to-hex slip (2500134 is 262626, not 2625A6) that turned 'the anchor has no text accent colour at all' into 'it has a link colour', weakening the argument it was cited for. Separately, rendering the artifact in a browser overturned three findings derived from CSS text, one of them simply wrong about a laptop.
tasks: Make the recount a step, not a virtue: any deliverable with more than five derived numbers gets a verification pass by something that cannot see the reasoning
Any claim about a rendered artifact stays inference until rendered. The cdp path works (native Chrome 9224 with --remote-allow-origins=*) and took four minutes; there was no excuse
A convention for marking a measured number apart from an inferred one inside a deliverable, so a reader can tell without reading a methods section
Extend tools/refute to accept a deliverable's numeric claims as falsifiers, so a review can be re-checked by running it rather than by re-reading it

epics.title: EPIC: Record where the plan was refuted, not only where the code failed
epics.body_intro: A red test says the code is wrong. A deviation from the plan says the plan was not buildable, and only the first has ever had a home in this repo. The second is regenerated and discarded every session. state/plan-deviations.jsonl was created 2026-07-31 and seeded with the two this session produced, both reconstructible only because they happened to be narrated in chat. Schema: ts, session, lane, plan, refuted_by, evidence, replan, class.
tasks: DONE 2026-07-31: ledger created and seeded with two rows. Row 1: the plan was to mask comments and string literals in panel.py; the planted selftest defect IS SQL inside a string literal, so masking would have turned the oracle green on a real injection. Row 2: the plan was to judge the deck from its CSS; rendering over CDP overturned three conclusions in four minutes
A capture command so recording a deviation costs one line, not a hand-edited JSONL row. Anything more expensive than narrating it will lose to narrating it
Wire it into the close-of-session path beside the handoff, so a session that replanned and did not record it is visible
Group by `class` after ten rows and see whether the classes recur. If they do, that is a premortem input; if they do not, the field is decoration and should be dropped

Decide whether a deviation belongs in state/lessons.jsonl instead. They are different: a lesson is a failure class, a deviation is a plan that could not survive contact. Keeping both only pays if the join is used

epics.title: EPIC: Fix data structures and interfaces before the first line of code
epics.body_intro: /premortem emits prose. Nothing in the planning path emits a signature, so interface decisions get made implicitly by whoever writes the first function. The measured cost: run_local in panel.py receives {file, line, text}, one diff line with no file handle. Nobody ratified that. Every 'it matched a comment' theory was downstream of it, three waivers were paid on that theory, and the real defect was that the line was not in the tree at all.
tasks: A planning stage that emits types and signatures, not paragraphs. Protocol classes or a .pyi is enough; the requirement is that the interface is reviewable before it is implemented
Retrofit the one that cost the most: decide explicitly whether run_local reviews a LINE or a FILE, and record the decision with its consequence for every check that reads context
Make /premortem's output include the signature block, so the failure modes it lists are attached to an interface rather than to an intention
Check the other oracles for the same unratified-interface shape: what does each one receive, and did anyone choose it

epics.title: EPIC: Run the artifact through a measurement function instead of rendering it
epics.body_intro: tools/e2e/flow.py drives another repo's running UI. There is no way to run OUR own artifact across all its states in a fast textual mode and read measurements out. Measured cost 2026-07-30: half a session inferring a deck's behaviour from its CSS, then four minutes over CDP to overturn three of those conclusions, including one that was simply wrong about a laptop.
tasks: A harness that takes an artifact, an enumerator of its N states, and a measurement function, and returns a table. The deck case was 31 slides through a per-slide probe
Port the CDP probe from this session into it as the first backend: launch, enumerate, measure, no screenshots unless a human asks
Second backend with no browser at all, for artifacts that have a textual state space, so the fast path does not depend on Chrome being installed
Acceptance: re-running it on thesis_story_9.html reproduces the takeaway-clipping table in section II.1b of the review without a human reading a screenshot

epics.title: EPIC: Adopt ast-grep so an oracle can tell code from prose about code
epics.body_intro: The class that cost three waivers is that a regex cannot separate code from prose about code. An AST can. ast-grep is Rust, tree-sitter based, YAML rules, and does the job panel.py does. Toolchain is present (cargo 1.97.1, rustc 1.97.1) and hookgate already bets on Rust with fancy-regex and serde_json. MoSCoW: ast-grep MUST; tree-sitter and tree-sitter-<lang> crates SHOULD, if the parse should live inside hookgate rather than shelling out; fd and tokei SHOULD for the repo sweep; hyperfine and sd COULD; GritQL via Biome WON'T yet, the plugin is beta with no autofixes.
tasks: cargo install ast-grep, then prove it in a SCRATCH rule file against the three sql-concat false positives and the planted selftest defect. Do not touch tools/hookgate: another session is mid-flight there and rewrote rules.rs once on 2026-07-31
Compare like for like: the two lookaheads now in panel.py against an ast-grep rule, on the same corpus. If the regex wins on this corpus, say so and stop
Decide the integration point: shell out to the ast-grep binary, or link tree-sitter into hookgate and keep one static binary. This is an interface decision and belongs to the signatures epic
Whichever wins, the selftest and a mutation control move with it. A new engine with no mutation proof is a downgrade regardless of how it matches

epics.title: EPIC: Repo Clear, an enforced standard rather than a written one
epics.body_intro: Survey 2026-07-31, walking the real tree because the interesting parts are gitignored: claude-setup 502 dirs / 11 empty / 1037 md / 106 byte-identical duplicates / 38 agent files. new-recruit 2822 dirs / 21 empty / 5717 md / 2479 duplicates (43 percent) / 193 agent files. daily-deep-learning 38 / 2 / 73 / 0. moneyballz 5 / 0 / 3 / 0. AGENTS.md is the standard to converge on: Linux Foundation AAIF stewardship, 60k+ repos, nearest file wins, no required sections. A prose standard rots; work-docs/research/README.md declares a lane the actual files ignore. So this ships as a checker with a gate domain.
tasks: tools/repoclear/scan.py, read-only: empty dirs, byte-identical duplicates, agent-file conflicts, build artifacts. One report over the four repos, zero deletions
One root AGENTS.md per repo written to the spec, nested only where a package genuinely differs. Superseded agent files get LISTED for removal, not removed
Wire repoclear as a gate domain on claude-setup first, with its own selftest and a mutation that must turn the selftest red

Fix the research output path while in there: every 2026-07-27 prompt states output lands in ~/docs/research/, which does not exist. The seven reports are in work-docs/ root under prose titles. Correct the path and add a check that fails when a prompt names a destination that does not exist

new-recruit dedup runs inventory first: hash pass, then near-duplicate pass reporting unique spans, then consolidation, and deletion only after a check proves no unique span was lost. Largest cluster first: 24 copies under projects/.axia-broken-worktree-retired-20260710
This blocks the WSL2 move (epic: WSL2 migration). Relocating 5717 markdown files of which 2479 are duplicates is paying to move garbage

epics.title: EPIC: The falsifier layer, and the five claims it now refutes
epics.body_intro: On 2026-07-31 `python tools/refute/refute.py run` reported `26 claims: 0 held, 0 REFUTED, 26 broken verifier`. One cause for all of them: every row declared `shell: "pwsh"` and neither pwsh nor powershell exists under WSL. The tool never lied about it, and it exits nonzero on unknowns, so nothing was falsely certified. What was lost was the layer itself, on the host the operator now works from. Repaired in aeaecd3; the run is now 21 held, 5 REFUTED, 0 broken. The five refutations below are the product and are deliberately NOT fixed in the commit that made them visible.
tasks: DONE 2026-07-31 (aeaecd3): shell `portable` is a real value AND the default; an unknown value is still BROKEN so this is not run-everything-and-hope. 19 of 26 rows needed only a shell that exists and forward slashes. 8 regression tests, all red before the fix; mutate --spec refute 12 of 12 caught.

DONE 2026-07-31: two of the seven PowerShell-native verifiers were AIMED WRONG, not merely unportable. They resolved $env:USERPROFILE\claude-setup, the Windows clone, a different working tree from the WSL one. With pwsh installed they would have reported on a checkout the session was not editing. checks/portable_claims.py anchors on its own file location instead.

DONE 2026-07-31: C-017 survived migration still carrying PowerShell. /bin/sh parsed it, choked on a brace, exited nonzero, and the runner correctly read nonzero as REFUTED. An infrastructure fault arrived dressed as a finding, in the one tool built to tell those apart. The test therefore checks the SOURCE for cmdlet syntax, not the exit code.

OPEN C-012: live ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is DELETED and settings.json was rewritten (7440b to 6807b) since the 2026-07-29 baseline. The global instruction file the harness reasons about is gone and nothing noticed for two days. OPERATOR DECISION: re-baseline, accepting the deletion as intended, or restore.

OPEN C-025: the pre-write snapshot for the pending settings.json write is INCOMPLETE, many agents/*.md MISSING, so that write is not revertable from it. A rollback source recorded as present and measured as partial.

OPEN C-003: 1 of 12 live hook registrations does not resolve. PreToolUse points at tools/hookgate/target/release/hookgate and the checker finds no script path there. A hook that cannot run fails open and reports nothing.
OPEN C-015: mutate --spec bus fails against the current tree, so bus.py's selftest is no longer proven able to fail.
OPEN C-008: hiring_engine/ledger.sqlite is absent at the path the claim names. Lane B owns that ledger, so this is a proposal row for B, not lane A work.

epics.title: EPIC: Bind the instruments that already run to a ratchet
epics.body_intro: Every defect the 2026-07-31 sweep found is one shape: a number that is produced and then bound to nothing that stops. docmap prints INDEX reachability at 3% and nothing fails. pointers.py counts 271 absent paths, exits FAIL, and is not a gate domain. skills_sync reports 49 drifted items and nothing fails. refute returned unknown 26 times for days. The proposal is a ratchet, a number that may not get worse, attached to checks that already run. Explicitly NOT a fourteenth gate domain: the count is already 13 and docs/reflections/2026-07-29-what-is-going-wrong.md section 4.2 warns against adding one.
tasks: BLOCKED on /diverge. This is a design decision and charters rule 2 requires five candidates with stated p_conventional before anything is built. Do not implement from this row.
Candidate surface, not a decision: the gate's `docs` domain already passes; a ratchet could live there rather than beside it.

docs/INDEX.md has no generator and nothing fails when it drifts, so its 113-of-114 coverage decays from the next document onward. Either generate it like CODEBASE-MAP and DOCMAP, or ratchet the reachability number docmap already computes. Do not do both.

8 of 18 specs declare no Status line. docmap passes them because it derives a class-based status, which answers what kind of document it is and never whether it is still true. The two architecture-build-plan files supersede each other by title and neither says so.
